translation.english_text: (With the playful Jolly beside him, Gunasekaran watches with distaste a dance taking place in a courtesan's house.)
notes: `தாசி வீடு` is rendered as `courtesan's house`; `ஜாலிக்காரி ஜாலி` carries a wordplay around Jolly's name that is only lightly reflected in English.

english_lines: O discerning gentleman, come!
Dressed in shining clothes,
Let us perform a joyous dance—when
We think of it, the heart
Sweetens; we know arts
That give delight and pleasure. (O discerning one
Seeing stone statues and paintings—and
Enchanted by their shapely beauty, by the sculpture's
Shapely beauty—do not, in vain,
Fill the mind with every fancy,
Rejoice in each as a marvel,
And sell away your reason—each day,
When you think of it, the heart
Sweetens; we know arts
That give delight and pleasure.
Seeking salvation in the heavenly world—millions
Have lost a life of pleasure—millions
Have lost the lives of women—merely
Standing in arrogance like a great sage,
Do not wander about in vain—each day,
When you think of it, the heart
Sweetens; we know arts
That give delight and pleasure.
notes: Semantic translation only; no singable metre or rhyme is introduced.
The source's compressed sequence around `பெண்களின் வாழ்க்கையை இழந்தவர்கள் கோடி` is translated conservatively rather than being silently rationalized.
The source refrain fragment `(ஓ ரசிகரும்` remains a cue rather than being reconstructed as a complete refrain.

source_locator.description: Jolly drugs Gunasekaran and takes his money.

translation.english_text: (At the dance performance, Jolly slips a stupefying drug into Gunasekaran's cold drink, renders him unconscious, and takes all his money.)
(After examining Kalyani.) Get this medicine urgently and bring it back.
(Seeing his father-in-law coming toward him.) How is she now?
(Showing the doctor's prescription.) Get this medicine urgently and bring it back. (Thangappan rides away quickly on his bicycle.)
(Coming outside.) A grandson, Panneerselvam, has been born.

(The son-in-law, on his way to buy the medicine, is struck by a car opposite the house, falls, and dies. His father-in-law, Manickam Pillai, witnesses it and dies from the shock. Kalyani becomes a widow.)
notes: The verified source explicitly includes `விழுந்து` (`falls`); the second-pass English restores that action rather than compressing it away.
